base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan their family Christmas dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any updates. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active guest's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates to people's health or restrictions throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm starting to plan our family Christmas dinner this year. It's going to be at my place. Any tips on putting together a menu?

flow_info.value: Six of us confirmed so far: me, my husband Tom, my sister Rachel, my mom Linda, and my brother-in-law Greg
Mom Linda was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes a couple years ago, she's been managing it with diet
Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last spring
Greg had a scary incident with peanut sauce at a Thai restaurant — throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Rachel just told me she's bringing her son Ethan, he's 4. He had a bad reaction to eggs last month — hives everywhere, pediatrician confirmed egg allergy
Trying to keep the whole dinner under $250 total, feeding 7 people

Rachel texted me this morning — she went back to her gastroenterologist last week and turns out she was misdiagnosed. She doesn't actually have celiac disease, her gut issues were from a medication she was on. She's totally fine with gluten now
Tom's been having gout flare-ups the past few weeks, doctor told him to stay away from red meat and organ meats for now
My Uncle Frank just called and asked if he could come too. Of course I said yes. He spent 20 years in Mumbai and converted — he's been practicing Jain for over a decade now
Mom just had her checkup and her A1C is completely normal now — doctor said she's no longer diabetic, doesn't need to restrict sugar anymore. She was so happy she cried
Greg just found out he has to work Christmas Day — he's a nurse and someone called in sick. He can't make dinner but asked if I could save him a plate to pick up later

Here's what I'm thinking for the menu: honey-glazed ham, roasted root vegetable medley with potatoes carrots and parsnips, green bean casserole with crispy onion topping, peanut butter chocolate pie, dinner rolls, and a classic egg nog

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (potatoes, carrots, onions, garlic, parsnips, turnips, beets, etc.)
constraints.surface_form: Uncle Frank spent 20 years in Mumbai and converted — he's been practicing Jain for over a decade now

Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Jain diet → no root vegetables (uprooting kills the plant)

hidden_state.value: You are planning a family Christmas dinner at your house. You will introduce the guest list and their health situations across several turns. Plans will change: a misdiagnosis gets corrected (celiac removed), your mom's diabetes resolves, a new uncle joins late with strict dietary needs, and one guest has to work but wants a plate saved. At the end you will share a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You must deliver the menu items exactly as listed and never hint at which dishes are problematic.

You are a calm, warm family organizer. You always refer to family members by name in third person (e.g. 'Rachel texted me...', 'Mom just told me...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing — you treat each update as normal holiday coordination. You are matter-of-fact, not overly enthusiastic.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family member updates

ground_truth.answer: Honey-glazed ham: problematic — ham is pork/meat, Uncle Frank is Jain (no meat); also Tom has gout (ham is arguably not red meat but is cured pork — borderline, but the primary issue is Uncle Frank). Roasted root vegetable medley (potatoes, carrots, parsnips): problematic for Uncle Frank — Jain diet forbids root vegetables (potatoes, carrots, parsnips are all roots). Green bean casserole with crispy onion topping: problematic for Uncle Frank — crispy onion topping contains root vegetable (onion). Green beans themselves are fine but the onion topping is not Jain-compliant. Peanut butter chocolate pie: problematic — contains peanut butter, Greg has severe peanut allergy and needs a saved plate, so this cannot be included on his plate. Also Uncle Frank cannot eat it if it contains eggs (most pies do). Dinner rolls: fine for everyone at the table (Rachel's celiac was a misdiagnosis, she can eat gluten now). Uncle Frank can eat bread if no eggs/root-derived ingredients. Egg nog: problematic — contains eggs, Ethan has egg allergy; also Uncle Frank is Jain (no eggs). Mom's diabetes restriction is gone — honey glaze and sugary pie are fine for her. Rachel's gluten restriction is gone — dinner rolls are fine for her.

Green bean casserole is problematic for Uncle Frank if it includes onion/garlic or crispy onion topping, since those are not Jain-compatible.
Peanut butter chocolate pie is problematic: contains peanuts, Greg has severe peanut allergy and his saved plate cannot include it
Egg nog is problematic: contains eggs, Ethan has an egg allergy; also Uncle Frank as Jain cannot consume eggs
Dinner rolls are fine — Rachel's celiac was a misdiagnosis, she can eat gluten now, so agent does not flag gluten as an issue
Mom Linda has no dietary restrictions anymore — agent does not flag sugar or honey glaze as a problem for her

Flagging honey-glazed ham or peanut butter chocolate pie as problematic for Mom due to sugar (her diabetes is resolved, A1C normal)
Ignoring Uncle Frank's Jain constraints on any dish (late-joining entity, must not be forgotten)
Saying Greg's peanut allergy no longer matters (he still needs a saved plate, peanut allergy applies to his plate)
Flagging any dish as problematic for Rachel due to gluten or celiac (misdiagnosis was corrected)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint removal across a 10-turn family Christmas dinner planning conversation. Key tracking challenges: (1) Uncle Frank joins late (aim_6) as a Jain — the agent must infer Jain → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables. This is the primary difficulty source as Jain root vegetable restrictions affect the root vegetable medley, the onion topping on the casserole, and potentially other dishes. (2) TWO constraint removals: Rachel's celiac is corrected as a misdiagnosis (aim_3), and Mom's diabetes resolves with normal A1C (aim_7). The agent must NOT flag gluten for Rachel or sugar for Mom. (3) Greg exits but wants a saved plate (aim_7) — his peanut allergy still applies to his plate, making peanut butter chocolate pie problematic for his portion. (4) Tom's gout (aim_4) means no red meat — ham is pork (not red meat in strict classification, but the primary ham issue is Uncle Frank's Jain constraint). (5) Ethan's egg allergy (aim_2) makes egg nog problematic. The probe includes 6 items with mixed verdicts: honey-glazed ham (bad — Uncle Frank Jain), root vegetable medley (bad — Uncle Frank Jain roots), green bean casserole (bad — onion topping is root for Uncle Frank), peanut butter chocolate pie (bad — Greg's peanut allergy for saved plate + Uncle Frank eggs), dinner rolls (FINE — trap, looks like gluten problem but Rachel's celiac was misdiagnosis), egg nog (bad — Ethan egg allergy + Uncle Frank Jain no eggs).

Green bean casserole's crispy onion topping is problematic for Uncle Frank: onions are root vegetables, forbidden under Jain diet
Peanut butter chocolate pie is problematic: contains peanuts, Greg has severe peanut allergy and his saved plate cannot include it
Egg nog is problematic: contains eggs, Ethan has an egg allergy; also Uncle Frank as Jain cannot consume eggs
